title: Far-infrared star formation rates of six GRB host galaxies with ALMA
question: Do rest-frame FIR ALMA continuum data change the SED-derived SFRs, stellar masses and AGN/radio requirements of six IR-bright z~2 GRB host galaxies compared with earlier work without FIR data

data.bands: Band 7, four spectral windows; average observed frequency 343.47925 GHz (873 um)
data.angular_resolution: Clean beam major axis 0.32-0.54 arcsec across the six hosts (Table 1)
data.sensitivity: Continuum sensitivities 0.04 uJy (2015.1.00927.S) and 0.02 uJy (2016.1.00768.S), as printed

what.value: UV-to-radio photometry of the six hosts (Tables 2 to 7), each row with its own reference

evidence.quote: We collected UV-to-radio photometric data of six GRB host galaxies reported in previous studies.

external_data.citation: Hunt2011; Svensson2012; Perley2013a; Perley2013b; Hunt2014; Perley2015; Kruhler2011; Hjorth2012; Jaunsen2008; Afonso2008; Michalowski2012; Postigo2012 (as listed per row in Tables 2-7)

what.value: GRB080207 host ALMA Band 9 flux density 11900 +/- 1700 uJy
GRB080207 host ALMA Band 8 flux density 3370 +/- 180 uJy
GRB080207 host ALMA Band 4 flux density 123.0 +/- 24 uJy

evidence.quote: The redshift of GRB060814 host galaxy was measured by (cite: Kruhler2012) to be $z=1.923$ by analysing several nebular emission lines in the near-infrared.
The redshift of the GRB was spectroscopically measured to be $z=2.260$ (cite: Salvaterra2012).
The redshift of GRB071021 was spectroscopically measured to be $z=2.452$ (cite: Kruhler2012).

what.value: Earlier SED-fit SFRs, stellar masses and IR luminosities used for comparison (Tables 12-13)

evidence.quote: The derived physical properties are compared with previous works

what.value: IMF conversion factors Salpeter to Chabrier: 0.61 for stellar mass and 0.63 for SFR

evidence.quote: Multiplied by a factor in (cite: Madau2014) (0.61 for stellar mass and 0.63 for SFR) from (cite: Salpeter1955) to (cite: Chabrier2003).

what.value: Effective wavelengths of photometric filters from the SVO Filter Profile Service

evidence.quote: This research has made use of the SVO Filter Profile Service

recipe.goal: Measure ALMA Band 7 continuum flux and position of each host
recipe.method: Fit the continuum images with CASA imfit to get flux, central position and errors
key_parameters: Input is the ASC-reduced data; fit region and component model not stated

recipe.method: Combine literature UV-to-radio photometry with the new Band 7 point; 3 sigma upper limits are not used in the fit; radio points are dropped in the no-radio configuration
key_parameters: Filter effective wavelengths from the SVO Filter Profile Service
assumptions: Radio emission may be contaminated by a long-lived radio afterglow

recipe.goal: Fit the SEDs with CIGALE under several configurations
recipe.method: CIGALE fits with sfh2exp or sfhdelayed SFH, bc03 SSP, nebular, power-law dust attenuation, Dale2014 dust+AGN (Draine2014 + Fritz2006 for GRB050915A) and redshifting modules; two IMFs (Salpeter, Chabrier); Group A fitted with/without AGN and with/without radio (4 configs), Group B with/without AGN (2 configs)
key_parameters: Module choices and parameter grids listed in Tables 8 and 9
assumptions: Single IMF per fit, Salpeter or Chabrier, chosen by reduced chi2

recipe.goal: Select best template and IMF per host
recipe.method: Best-fit template chosen by reduced chi2 (closest to 1); fits with reduced chi2 well below 1 treated as over-fits and their AGN component rejected

recipe.goal: Cross-check SED SFRs with the Kennicutt IR-luminosity relation
recipe.method: Convert the CIGALE dust luminosity to SFR with the Kennicutt (1998) relation and compare with SED SFRs
key_parameters: L_IR integrated 8 to 1000 um in the Kennicutt definition

recipe.goal: Compare with earlier SED fits after IMF conversion
recipe.method: Convert earlier results to Chabrier IMF (Salpeter divided by 1.8 or 1.6 in the literature) and convert this work's Salpeter results with Madau & Dickinson factors, then tabulate differences
key_parameters: 0.61 for stellar mass and 0.63 for SFR
